hints.content:
The function $f$ is positive $($i.e. $f(x)>0)$ whenever its graph is above the $x$-axis.

This is because the positive $y$-values are above the $x$-axis, and $y=f(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by one-half. The graph of the function y equals f of x is above the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative three. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative three to x equals zero. It is above the x-axis from x equals zero to x equals three. It is below the x-axis from x equals three to five. The function is decreasing from x equals negative five to x equals negative one and one-half. The function increases from x equals negative one and one-half to x equals one and one-half. The function increases from x equals one and one-half to x equals five. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative three and from x equals zero to x equals three.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $1<x<2$.
